mainTopic: The ban on non-Jewish oil: its source (שמואל's vessels or רב's דניאל), its place among the שמונה עשר דבר, and how רבי יהודה הנשיא could permit it
overview: The גמרא explains שמואל's reason for the ban on non-Jewish oil: the oil soaks up forbidden food from the non-Jew's vessels. שמואל says this fits a report that רבי יהודה הנשיא and his בית דין voted to permit the oil, because נותן טעם לפגם is מותר. But on רב's view, that דניאל decreed the ban, a later court should not have been able to cancel it. רב first questions the witness, and then brings a פסוק showing that דניאל avoided oil. The two agree that דניאל kept away from oil, but they argue whether he made it a rule for all ישראל. The גמרא then reconciles רב with a teaching in his own name that counts oil among the שמונה עשר דבר. Its answer is that דניאל banned oil in the city, and the students of שמאי and הלל extended the ban to the field. Last, it explains how רבי יהודה הנשיא could permit oil even though the שמונה עשר דבר are normally permanent: the oil ban never spread among most of ישראל, and a decree must be one that most of the community can keep. The amud ends by asking for the פסוק behind that rule, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל's first reason: drippings from impure vessels
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's reason for forbidding non-Jewish oil is first quoted as the drippings of טמא vessels that soak into the oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: The drippings of impure vessels make the oil forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes שמואל's reason for the ban on non-Jewish oil: what oozes out of impure vessels gets into the oil and forbids it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב had given a different reason, that the ban was a decree of דניאל. שמואל instead points to the vessels the oil sits in. This first version says the problem is טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: drippings or oozing; what comes out of a vessel's walls into what is stored inside

phrases.english: The drippings of ritually impure vessels
phrases.notes: This is about the oil non-Jews pour into their vessels; the vessel walls seep into the oil.

phrases.english: make them forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives שמואל's reason for the oil ban, as opposed to רב's reason (a decree of דניאל) from just before this text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Non-Jewish oil is forbidden because of the drippings of impure vessels.

steps.title: But not everyone eats only pure food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the impurity reason: most people are allowed to eat טמא food, so impurity cannot explain a general ban.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that everyone eats only pure food?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the version of שמואל's reason it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating טמא food is allowed for most people. Only someone who keeps טהרות, who carefully eats only pure food, would care about טומאה. So טומאה cannot be the reason for a ban that applies to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: is that to say...? (a challenging question)
people who eat only ritually pure food

phrases.english: Is that to say that all people
are eaters of pure food?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אוֹכְלֵי טְהָרוֹת נִינְהוּ
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that impure vessels are the reason for the oil ban.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: טומאה only matters to people who eat טהרות. A ban that applies to everyone cannot rest on it.

steps.title: Corrected reason: drippings from forbidden vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects שמואל's wording: the problem is vessels that held forbidden food, not impure vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the drippings of forbidden vessels make the oil forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes שמואל's statement so it makes sense. The vessels had absorbed non-kosher food, and that seeps into the oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing one word, from טמאים to אסורין, turns the reason into a question of כשרות, which applies to everyone. Now the problem is forbidden taste, not impurity.

phrases.english: Rather, the drippings of forbidden vessels
make them forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, זְלִיפָתָן שֶׁל כֵּלִים אֲסוּרִין אוֹסַרְתָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 2 by correcting the wording of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the statement
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל's reason is absorbed forbidden food, which applies to everyone.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's real reason: the oil absorbs forbidden taste from the non-Jew's vessels. רב's reason: דניאל decreed against it.

steps.title: שמואל: my view explains why רבי יהודה permitted the oil
steps.stepSummary: שמואל tells רב that his own reason fits a report that רבי יהודה הנשיא and his בית דין voted to permit the oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to רב: On my view, that the drippings of forbidden vessels forbid the oil, I can understand the report of רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא. He said that רבי שמלאי taught in נציבין that רבי יהודה and his בית דין voted on the oil and permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל brings a report that the ban on oil was later lifted. He says this report fits his own view, and he is setting up a challenge to רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ban rested on a reason about taste, a later בית דין could rethink that reason and permit the oil. The explanation of why comes in the next step. This opens the attack on רב.

keyTerms.meaning: granted, it makes sense (sets up a contrast with the other view)
they were counted, meaning they took a vote

phrases.english: שמואל said to רב:
Granted, according to me, who says
that the drippings of forbidden vessels make the oil forbidden,
this is why, when there came

phrases.aramaic: רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָא וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא, he said:
רבי שמלאי taught in נציבין:
Regarding oil, רבי יהודה and his court
voted on it and permitted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the corrected reason from step 3 as the basis for an argument against רב.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's reason for the oil ban (forbidden vessels).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The report through רבי שמלאי that רבי יהודה הנשיא's בית דין permitted the oil.

steps.title: Why רבי יהודה permitted it: flavor that spoils is allowed
steps.stepSummary: On שמואל's view, רבי יהודה permitted the oil because he held that נותן טעם לפגם is מותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: something that gives a bad taste is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains how רבי יהודה could permit the oil on his view. The taste the oil picks up from the vessels makes it worse, not better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A forbidden taste only forbids a food when it improves it. Old forbidden taste from the vessel walls only spoils the oil, so the oil stays permitted. This is a reason a later בית דין could judge for itself.

keyTerms.meaning: gives a taste that spoils the food

steps.whyThisMatters: נותן טעם לפגם is a basic rule in the laws of mixing forbidden food and in the laws of vessels.

phrases.english: He holds: something that gives a spoiling taste is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי יהודה's ruling in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה held that נותן טעם לפגם is מותר, so the vessels' taste does not forbid the oil.

steps.title: On רב's view, how could a later court cancel דניאל's decree?
steps.stepSummary: שמואל challenges רב: if דניאל made the decree, רבי יהודה הנשיא could not cancel it, since a court must be greater in wisdom and number to cancel an earlier court's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: But on your view, that דניאל decreed against the oil, could רבי יהודה הנשיא come and cancel what דניאל decreed? We learned in a משנה: a court cannot cancel the words of another court unless it is greater in wisdom and in number!
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל turns to רב's view and shows that it cannot explain why רבי יהודה permitted the oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A decree is a ruling of a בית דין, and a later בית דין may cancel it only if it is greater in wisdom and in number. רבי יהודה's court was not greater than דניאל's. So on רב's view the permission makes no sense.
steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the oil itself. It is about whether a later court has the power to cancel an earlier court's decree.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key rule about the authority of rabbinic decrees. The גמרא will need to answer it to defend רב.

phrases.english: But according to you, who said
that דניאל decreed against it,
phrases.notes: This is רב's reason from just before this, that the ban on non-Jewish oil comes from דניאל.

phrases.english: דניאל decreed, and then came
רבי יהודה הנשיא and cancels it?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
A court cannot cancel
the words of another court,
unless it is greater than it
in wisdom and in number!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְדִידָךְ דְּאָמְרַתְּ דָּנִיאֵל גָּזַר עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the בשלמא argument begun in step 4: it works for שמואל but not for רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that the oil ban was a decree of דניאל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A later court may cancel an earlier decree only if it is greater in wisdom and number. רבי יהודה's court was not greater than דניאל's, so it could not have permitted the oil if רב is right.

steps.title: רב questions the witness from לוד
steps.stepSummary: רב does not answer שמואל's challenge directly. Instead he attacks the report itself, saying people from לוד are not careful with rabbinic decrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: Are you talking about שמלאי from לוד? People from לוד are different, because they treat the decrees of the חכמים lightly.
steps.whatsHappening: רב tries to knock out the report that רבי יהודה הנשיא permitted the oil by questioning the person who reported it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's challenge in step 6 depends on the report that רבי יהודה הנשיא permitted the oil. If the witness, שמלאי of לוד, is unreliable, the report falls away and so does the challenge. רב says people from לוד take decrees lightly, so their testimony about a permit is suspect.

keyTerms.meaning: שמלאי from the town of לוד, the one who reported the permit
They treat lightly, they take rabbinic rules casually

phrases.english: He said to him
Is it Simlai of Lod you are talking about?
The people of Lod are different, because they treat [the decrees] lightly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by undercutting the report it relies on.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reliability of the testimony that רבי יהודה הנשיא permitted the oil.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The witness comes from לוד, where people are lax about rabbinic decrees.

steps.title: שמואל offers to bring the witness, and רב is embarrassed
steps.stepSummary: שמואל offers to send for שמלאי himself. רב is embarrassed, which shows his attack on the witness does not hold up.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to him: Should I send for him? רב was embarrassed.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל pushes back on רב's attack by offering to bring the witness in person. רב has no answer and is embarrassed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By offering to call שמלאי, שמואל shows the report can be confirmed directly, so the rumor about לוד does not matter. רב's embarrassment shows his rejection of the witness has failed. The report that רבי יהודה הנשיא permitted the oil stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Should I send for him? (bring him here to confirm)

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Now שמואל is speaking to רב.

phrases.english: Should I send for him?
He was embarrassed.
phrases.notes: It is רב who is embarrassed, since his attack on the witness did not work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב's rejection of the witness, so the report stays in place.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב's claim that the report from לוד is unreliable.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The witness can be brought and asked directly, so a general suspicion about his town proves nothing.

steps.title: רב brings a verse showing דניאל avoided oil
steps.stepSummary: רב says that even if רבי יהודה הנשיא's court did not learn it from the פסוק, we must. The plural word משתיו in דניאל points to two kinds of drink, wine and oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: If they did not learn it from the פסוק, should we not learn it? It is written: "And דניאל set it on his heart that he would not make himself impure with the king's food and with the wine of his drinkings." The פסוק is talking about two drinkings: one of wine and one of oil.
steps.whatsHappening: רב admits the permit happened but says that court missed a פסוק. He brings a פסוק showing that דניאל kept away from oil of גוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word משתיו ("his drinkings") is plural, so רב reads the פסוק as speaking of two kinds of drinking: one of wine and one of oil. This supports רב's view that the oil ban goes back to דניאל.

keyTerms.meaning: They expounded, they learned a law out of a פסוק
The king's food, his rich food
His drinkings (plural), the key word of the proof

steps.confusionAlert: Oil is called a 'drink' here only because of how the plural word is read. The proof rests on the plural form of משתיו, not on oil normally being something people drink.

phrases.english: Rav said:
If they did not expound,
phrases.notes: 'They' means רבי יהודה הנשיא and his בית דין, who permitted the oil.

phrases.english: shall we not expound?
But isn't it written:
"And Daniel set upon his heart
that he would not defile himself
with the king's food
and with the wine of his drinkings"
the verse speaks of two drinkings:
one is the drinking of wine
and one is the drinking of oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם הֵם לֹא דָּרְשׁוּ, אֲנַן לָא דָּרְשִׁינַן? וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the attack on the witness fails, רב supports his position from a פסוק instead.
steps.raayaObject: רב's position that דניאל was the source of the ban on oil of גוים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דניאל 1:8, where the plural משתיו is read as wine and oil.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רב accepts that the permit happened. He argues that the permitting court overlooked a scriptural source.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree whether דניאל taught all ישראל
steps.stepSummary: Both agree that דניאל avoided oil himself. They argue over whether he made it a rule for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב held: דניאל set it on his heart and taught it to all of ישראל. שמואל held: he set it on his heart but did not teach it to all of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how שמואל can accept רב's פסוק and still hold that the oil was not forbidden by דניאל's decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words על לבו ("on his heart") can mean a private commitment. For רב, דניאל also made it binding on everyone, so it was a real decree. For שמואל, it stayed a personal stringency, so no earlier court's decree stood in רבי יהודה הנשיא's way.

keyTerms.meaning: He set it upon his heart, he took it on himself
He taught, he ruled for others

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees דניאל avoided oil of גוים. The only argument is whether this was his personal practice (שמואל) or a decree for all ישראל (רב).

phrases.english: Rav held:
he set it upon his heart,
and he taught it to all Israel;
and Shmuel held:
he set it upon his heart,
but he did not teach it to all Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב סָבַר: עַל לִבּוֹ שָׂם, וּלְכׇל יִשְׂרָאֵל הוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why שמואל is not moved by רב's proof from the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both agree on the reading of the פסוק but disagree about how far it reaches (a personal practice or a public decree).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to prove that דניאל decreed the oil ban for everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: For שמואל, the פסוק shows only דניאל's personal practice, so רבי יהודה הנשיא was not overturning an earlier court's decree.

steps.title: Challenge: רב himself counts oil among the eighteen decrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether דניאל really decreed against oil, since a teaching in רב's own name lists oil among the שמונה עשר דבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And oil, did דניאל decree it? But באלי said that אבימי of נותא said in the name of רב: their bread and their oil, their wine and their daughters, all of these are from the שמונה עשר דבר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's position by quoting a statement in רב's own name that seems to contradict it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the oil ban is one of the שמונה עשר דבר, it was made by a later court, not by דניאל. That contradicts רב's claim in step 10 that דניאל decreed it for all ישראל. So רב appears to contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Their (the גוים') bread and their oil
The eighteen decrees made together on one day

phrases.english: And oil, did Daniel decree it?
But didn't Balei say
[that] Avimi of Nota [said] in the name of Rav:
Their bread and their oil,
their wine and their daughters,
all of them are from the eighteen matters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's position from step 10 that דניאל decreed the oil ban.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that דניאל forbade oil of גוים for all ישראל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A statement in רב's own name lists oil among the שמונה עשר דבר, which were decreed much later. That suggests דניאל was not the source of the ban.

steps.title: Maybe דניאל's decree was simply not accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that דניאל decreed against oil but nobody accepted it, and later the students of הלל and שמאי decreed it again and it stuck. It rejects this, because then רב's report about דניאל would mean nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might say: דניאל decreed, but people did not accept it. Later the students of הלל and שמאי decreed it, and people accepted it. But if so, what is the point of רב's testimony?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible answer to the question from step 11 and immediately knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested answer would explain why oil is counted among the שמונה עשר דבר: the decree only took hold in the students' time. But then רב's claim that the ban came from דניאל would add nothing, since דניאל's decree would have had no effect. So this answer cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a possible answer)
The students of שמאי and הלל

phrases.english: And if you would say:
Daniel came and decreed, but it was not accepted,
and the students of Hillel and Shammai came
and decreed, and it was accepted,
if so, what is the point of Rav's testimony?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: אֲתָא דָּנִיאֵל גְּזַר וְלָא קַיבֻּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and rejects a possible answer to the challenge in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested answer that דניאל's decree simply failed
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would make רב's testimony about דניאל meaningless.

steps.title: דניאל banned oil in the city, the students banned it even in the field
steps.stepSummary: The real answer: דניאל's decree covered oil in the city, and the students of שמאי and הלל widened it to include the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, דניאל decreed against it in the city. Then they came and decreed against it even in the field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its real answer to step 11: there were two decrees, and the second one went further than the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both sources are true. רב is right that דניאל started the ban, and the teaching is right that oil is among the שמונה עשר דבר. The students added a wider version of the ban that also covers the field.
steps.whatToRemember: Gentile oil: דניאל banned it in the city, and the students of שמאי and הלל extended the ban to the field.

phrases.english: Rather, Daniel decreed against it in the city,
and they came and decreed against it even in the field.
phrases.notes: "They" are the students of שמאי and הלל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting into two decrees with different scope
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that only one of them could be the source of the ban, either דניאל or the students.
steps.terutzMaskana: דניאל banned oil in the city, and the students extended the ban to the field.

steps.title: How could רבי יהודה הנשיא cancel a decree of the students?
steps.stepSummary: If the students of שמאי and הלל made a decree on oil, how could רבי יהודה הנשיא permit it? A משנה says a court cannot cancel another court's words unless it is greater in wisdom and number.
steps.simpleTranslation: How could רבי יהודה הנשיא permit an enactment of the students of שמאי and הלל? We learned in a משנה: a court cannot cancel the words of another court unless it is greater than it in wisdom and in number!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem that comes from the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the oil ban belongs to the students of שמאי and הלל, permitting it means cancelling another court's decree. The משנה allows that only if the later court is greater in wisdom and in number. רבי יהודה הנשיא's court was not greater than theirs.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi,
how could he permit
an enactment of the students of Shammai and Hillel?
But didn't we learn in a Mishnah:
A court cannot cancel
the words of another court,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן גָּדוֹל הֵימֶנּוּ בְּחָכְמָה וּבְמִנְיָן!
phrases.english: unless it is greater than it in wisdom and in number!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא הֵיכִי מָצֵי לְמִישְׁרֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The answer in step 13 creates a new problem with רבי יהודה הנשיא's permission of oil.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה הנשיא's court permitting gentile oil
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A later court cannot cancel an earlier court's decree unless it is greater in wisdom and number.

steps.title: The שמונה עשר דבר can never be cancelled
steps.stepSummary: There is an even stronger problem. רבי יוחנן says the שמונה עשר דבר can never be cancelled, not even by אליהו and his court.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a court can cancel another court's words in everything, except the eighteen matters. Even if אליהו and his court came to cancel them, we would not listen to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger challenge to the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first challenge left room for a greater court to cancel a decree. This second one closes that door: the שמונה עשר דבר are permanent no matter who the later court is. Since oil is one of them, permitting it seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: The eighteen decrees made by the students of שמאי and הלל

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד, הָא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
phrases.english: And furthermore, didn't Rabba bar bar Chana say
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
In everything, a court can cancel
the words of another court,
except for the eighteen matters,
for even if Eliyahu and his court came
phrases.notes: He means: came to cancel them.

phrases.english: we would not listen to him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, הָא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה הנשיא's court permitting gentile oil
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The שמונה עשר דבר can never be cancelled, even by the greatest court, and oil is one of them.

steps.title: The ban on oil never spread among most of ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא explains that the שמונה עשר דבר cannot be cancelled because they spread among most of ישראל. The ban on oil never spread that way, so it could be cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: What is the reason the eighteen matters cannot be cancelled? Because their prohibition spread among most of ישראל. But the prohibition of oil did not spread among most of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא answers both challenges by explaining why the eighteen decrees are normally permanent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decrees cannot be cancelled because most of the people actually took them on. Oil is still one of the eighteen, but it is an exception: its ban never caught on among most people. So the reason that makes the decrees permanent does not apply to oil, and רבי יהודה הנשיא could permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: The majority of the Jewish people

steps.confusionAlert: Oil is not being removed from the list of the שמונה עשר דבר. It is still one of them; it is just an exception to the rule that they can never be cancelled.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why רבי יהודה הנשיא could permit gentile oil even though it was one of the שמונה עשר דבר.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said: What is the reason?
Because its prohibition spread among most of Israel.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמֶן לֹא פָּשַׁט אִיסּוּרוֹ בְּרוֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: But oil, its prohibition did not spread among most of Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges of steps 14 and 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the reason behind the rule and showing it does not apply here
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All eighteen decrees, including oil, can never be cancelled.
steps.terutzMaskana: The eighteen are permanent because they spread among most of Israel. Oil's ban did not spread, so it could be cancelled.

steps.title: The Rabbis checked and found the oil ban had not spread
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports that the Rabbis investigated and found the oil ban had not spread among most of ישראל. They relied on the rule that a decree is only made if most of the community can keep it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי שמואל בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Our Rabbis sat and checked about oil, and found that its prohibition had not spread among most of ישראל. They relied on the words of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי אלעזר בר צדוק, who used to say: we do not make a decree on the community unless most of the community can keep it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רב משרשיא's claim that the ban on oil never spread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a report of what actually happened: the Rabbis investigated and found that most people were not keeping the ban. They based their decision to permit oil on an old rule: a decree that most people cannot keep should not stand.

keyTerms.meaning: To keep it, to live up to it

steps.whatToRemember: A decree is only made if most of the community can keep it. The oil ban did not meet that test, so it could be permitted.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Shmuel bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Our Rabbis sat and checked about oil
and found that its prohibition had not spread among most of Israel,

phrases.aramaic: וְסָמְכוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ עַל דִּבְרֵי רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: and our Rabbis relied on the words of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק,
phrases.english: and on the words of Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok,
who used to say:
We do not make a decree on the community

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן רוֹב צִבּוּר יְכוֹלִין לַעֲמוֹד בָּהּ,
phrases.english: unless most of the community is able to keep it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן

steps.raayaObject: That the oil ban never spread among most of Israel, and so could be permitted

steps.title: Looking for the פסוק behind the rule
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה asks which פסוק teaches that a decree is only made if most of the community can keep it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב אדא בר אהבה said: What is the verse?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to show the פסוק that supports the rule from step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a decree needs most of the community to be able to keep it now gets a source in the תנ"ך. The answer comes in the next part of the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse? (asks for the source in a פסוק)

phrases.english: As Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
What is the verse?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: מַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule cited in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches a decree is only made if most of the community can keep it.
